se-01TK.title: Roofs: grey diamond tiles
se-01TK.summary: Grey diamond-tiled roofs in the far south, south-east coast and the Baltic islands. West and south houses use stone and brick, the north-east uses red painted wood.

se-0ZfL.title: Markers: small red crosses on snowmobile trails
se-0ZfL.summary: Small red crosses marking snowmobile trails appear across the northern half.

se-1W0U.title: Houses: big red farmhouses with many windows
se-1W0U.summary: Big, mostly red farmhouses of 2 to 3 floors with many large windows and a long grand front. Even barns have lots of windows.

se-1kzH.title: Road: dramatic mountains, big lake on the south
se-1kzH.summary: A small, well-paved road without road lines, with a large lake on the south and some of the most dramatic mountains on Street View here. Covered in summer and early spring.

se-3eFT.title: Bus stops: neon-yellow school bus signs
se-3eFT.summary: Neon-yellow school bus stop signs in three east-central municipalities.

se-3eeu.title: Plants: neat rows of thin birches in towns, north coast
se-3eeu.summary: Long neat rows of moderately thin birches in towns on the north coast.

se-41YA.title: Landscape: island with lake on both sides
se-41YA.summary: An island in a big southern lake: farm fields with the lake visible to the north-west and south-east and forested hills on both shores.

se-43GR.title: Google car: white Gen 3 car with a visual glitch
se-43GR.summary: A small northern island has Gen 3 coverage from a white car with a long antenna and a distinctive visual glitch. A similar but weaker glitch exists elsewhere.

se-48zT.title: Pole: orange snow poles with two wide reflectors
se-48zT.summary: In mountains, orange snow poles with two wide reflectors close together mean near the Norwegian border on or near road E12.

se-4Tj8.title: Street signs: -vägen and -gatan endings
se-4Tj8.summary: Street names end in 'vägen' and 'gatan', often shortened to v and g. 'Gränd' appears near city centres. Norway uses vei or gate, and Denmark vej and gade.

differs.how: Norway uses vei or gate, attached to the name
Denmark uses vej and gade

se-4jd6.title: Sheds: octagonal or leaning-wall red log sheds
se-4jd6.summary: On the northern coast, farm sheds are octagonal or rectangular with walls leaning outwards, usually red-painted logs.

se-5aMv.title: Bollard: cylinder with horizontal black band
se-5aMv.summary: Cylindrical bollards with a fully horizontal black section near the top, mostly near the west coast and in two central counties.

se-5ceh.title: Road: red dirt and water smudges on camera
se-5ceh.summary: A road on the border of two counties has slightly red dirt and several water smudges on the camera. Look for the 'Reindeer spot point' on the county border.

se-5n8T.title: Objects: red and yellow roadworks and barriers
se-5n8T.summary: Lots of road equipment is painted red and yellow, including roadwork signs, blocks and even chevrons.

se-76UZ.title: Landscape: flat fields with small round forested hills
se-76UZ.summary: On the west coast, flat fields with small round forested hills in the distance. Hills get bigger and fields smaller going north. It is lush from the rain.

se-7nZT.title: Plants: broad-leaved trees only in the south
se-7nZT.summary: Broad-leaved trees other than birch grow naturally only in the southern half, and get more common going south.

se-8cKu.title: Trams: mostly in the second city
se-8cKu.summary: Trams show up mostly in the west-coast big city, then two other cities, and rarely in Gen 4 in a southern university town.

se-91Xp.title: Road: grey sandy ground, moss, ditch, low forest
se-91Xp.summary: The northern part of road 99 has grey sandy ground with brown-green moss, a clear ditch beside the road and low dense forest of birch, pine and spruce. The latest coverage is early spring.

se-9JTA.title: Flags: yellow flag, red cross, crown
se-9JTA.summary: The church flag is a red cross on yellow with a crown in the middle, often near churches.

se-9Rd5.title: Bollard: small white with blue or red band
se-9Rd5.summary: Small white bollards with a blue or red strip near the top in the far south countryside, occasionally in towns further north.

se-9XCt.title: Sign: railway crossing back sticker, first digit region
se-9XCt.summary: The back of railway crossing signs has a yellow sticker with a 5-digit ID. The first digit is the region and mostly rises to the north-east. A 6 can appear randomly almost anywhere.

se-9iUB.title: Roads: deep grey dirt road, green grass
se-9iUB.summary: Deep grey dirt roads with low green grass on both sides, in the northern half of one mid-north county, in Gen 4 summer and Gen 3 autumn.

se-A5tj.title: Plants: ferns in south and centre
se-A5tj.summary: Ferns are mostly in the south and centre, occasionally further north in the east.

se-AK7h.title: Plate: long white, taxis yellow
se-AK7h.summary: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left. Taxi plates have a yellow background.

se-AWak.title: Bus stops: city and town specific signs
se-AWak.summary: Many cities and towns have their own bus stop signs, different from the region's. One city's sign also appears in a nearby town.

se-B5Nf.title: Landscape: boreal forest, farms, lakes
se-B5Nf.summary: Lots of boreal forest, small to medium farmland and many lakes. The north and west are mountainous with long narrow lakes and rivers, the south and east flatter.

se-BYNl.title: Houses: grey metal roofs more common north
se-BYNl.summary: Grey metal roofs on homes get more common going north. Barn and shed metal roofs appear much further south.

se-BgHS.title: Google car: white car, long antenna, Gen 3
se-BgHS.summary: A white car with a long antenna in much of the Gen 3 coverage. Iceland has it on all roads, Finland fairly often, Norway and Denmark extremely rarely.

se-BvIc.title: Landscape: coastal road, rocky beach, low bushes
se-BvIc.summary: A small coastal road on the north-west coast of one flat island, with a rocky beach and low bushy plants.

se-Dbca.title: Street signs: blue with thin black outline
se-Dbca.summary: Blue street signs with a thin black outline in one central town.

se-FJkx.title: Sign: blue sign with big white M
se-FJkx.summary: Small roads often have blue signs with a large white M, a passing place. Norway has similar ones in a different font, where the middle of the M goes to the bottom. Finland has none.

differs.how: Norwegian M is a different font, middle reaches the bottom

se-GAXT.title: Town: old stone houses over narrow cobbled alleys
se-GAXT.summary: The capital's old town has old stone buildings in warm colours towering over narrow cobblestone alleys.

se-GCla.title: Google car: red, white or blue Gen 4 car
se-GCla.summary: Gen 4 has three cars: red, white and blue, each with or without a visible antenna. Only the blue one is in Norway, Finland and Denmark.

differs.how: Only the blue car exists there
Only the blue car exists there
Only the blue car exists there

se-GIKf.title: Houses: blue or green slag stone
se-GIKf.summary: Buildings fully or partly of blue or green slag stone can occasionally be found in an old mining region.

se-GOZR.title: Language: Finnish-like Meänkieli near the border
se-GOZR.summary: A language close to Finnish near the Finnish border, often on river signs ending in 'väylä'. Trilingual signs with Sámi exist. Finnish-sounding place names mean you are near that border.

se-GU16.title: Houses: dark red wooden countryside houses
se-GU16.summary: Countryside houses are mostly wooden, often painted dark red. Almost only Sweden, Norway and Finland use this paint. Towns are modern concrete and brick, suburbs have detached wood or brick houses.

se-HBIA.title: Landscape: smooth mountain with low treeline
se-HBIA.summary: In the northern mining town you often see a smooth-sloped mountain with a low treeline to the south-west. No other town has a natural treeless mountain so close.

se-HT91.title: Landscape: most open farmland, many crops
se-HT91.summary: The most open farmland: only small patches of trees across the fields instead of dense forest. Crops are more varied than the usual cereals.

se-IsNb.title: Houses: half-timbered
se-IsNb.summary: Half-timbered houses, mainly in the southern half of the far-south region, also its northern half and south-west coast. Rarely in the walled island town.

se-Ixwk.title: Town: cobblestones, colourful houses, roses
se-Ixwk.summary: The only preserved medieval trading-league town: cobblestone streets, small brightly painted stone houses, roses on walls and the old wall around it.

se-JUZe.title: Sign: red border, plain yellow background
se-JUZe.summary: Road signs have a red border and yellow background. Finland adds a thin yellow border outside the red one.

differs.how: Finnish signs have a thin yellow outer border

se-KMWO.title: Houses: pale white and light yellow on west coast
se-KMWO.summary: Houses are usually colourful, but on the west coast they are much lighter, with many white and light yellow ones between the second city and the Norwegian border.

se-Kd2Q.title: Route numbers: national 9-99, regional 100-404
se-Kd2Q.summary: Besides European highways: national roads 9-99 and regional roads 100-404. Numbers tend to rise going north-east, but the maps are approximate.

se-Kgx2.title: Bus stops: regional bus shelter designs
se-Kgx2.summary: Many regions have their own bus shelters, shown in the image. Each region has several types.

se-LTfr.title: Bus stops: each region has its own sign
se-LTfr.summary: Each region has at least one bus stop sign unique to it, shown in the image.

se-LvtG.title: Landscape: extremely flat island, many small rock walls
se-LvtG.summary: An extremely flat island: barren south half with many small bushes, slightly lusher north with fewer, larger bushes and trees. Very many small rock walls.

se-N8or.title: Landscape: large grass farmland in wide steep hills
se-N8or.summary: Large farmland sitting among wide, fairly steep hills, mostly ordinary uncultivated grass. Elsewhere farmland is on flat ground or in valleys.

se-NWKo.title: Houses: old factory towns, rows of identical houses
se-NWKo.summary: Near the coast north and east of one big city, old factory towns with long rows of identical houses in bright stone or red wood, small belfries, mansions and factories in the same style.

se-Nhg0.title: Sign: blue direction signs, white text
se-Nhg0.summary: Mostly blue with white text and border and a thin arrow. Yellow signs with black text and red border are common too, for tiny places. Norway uses yellow or white, and Finland a filled arrow.

differs.how: Norwegian signs are yellow or white
Finnish signs have a filled white arrow

se-OvOv.title: Statues: dragon city dragons
se-OvOv.summary: One east-coast city calls itself the Dragon City and has dragon statues in its centre and on signs.

se-SsmQ.title: Roads: red dirt roads
se-SsmQ.summary: Red dirt roads are mostly in one central-west county, also in the south-east, between two northern counties, and rarely between the two big southern lakes.

se-TMZ2.title: Language: Å, Ä and Ö
se-TMZ2.summary: Letters Å, Ä and Ö. Danish and Norwegian have Å but not Ä or Ö, Icelandic has Ö only. Finnish has Ä and Ö but longer words with double vowels.

differs.how: Finnish words are longer with double vowels
Norwegian has Å but no Ä or Ö
Danish has Å but no Ä or Ö

se-TkCB.title: Street signs: plain bright yellow
se-TkCB.summary: Plain yellow street signs in one west town. Very rarely elsewhere, but always a clearly brighter yellow.

se-Ugnu.title: Plants: beech forest, brown leaves on bare ground
se-Ugnu.summary: Beech forests, with barren ground covered in brown leaves, are mainly in the far south.

se-UzEZ.title: Landscape: fields through small valleys
se-UzEZ.summary: Farm fields often run through small valleys with forest on the sides. Fields are medium to small.

se-Wh27.title: Pole: orange snow pole, tall white reflector
se-Wh27.summary: Orange snow pole with a tall white reflector a bit above the middle, sometimes with a thinner second reflector. Finnish poles have a thin reflector near the top, Norwegian ones one or two thinner reflectors.

differs.how: Reflector is thin and close to the top
One or two thinner reflectors, one often near the middle

se-WhIN.title: Landscape: stepped mine-made mountains
se-WhIN.summary: In the far-north mining town you often see one of two mountains shaped by the mine, one south and one north, with staircase-like layers on the side.

se-WoV2.title: Google car: white car with a blue stripe on the back
se-WoV2.summary: A white car with a blue stripe on the back appears along the west coast and in the far south. It is almost never found outside the country.

se-YHDK.title: Road lines: solid outer line made of small pieces
se-YHDK.summary: Highway outer lines look solid from far away but are split into small sections in a unique pattern. Denmark's look similar, but its pieces are rectangular.

differs.how: Danish sections are rectangular
Finland's line is truly solid
Norway's line is truly solid

se-YJez.title: Soil: white sand beside roads
se-YJez.summary: White sand beside roads, mostly in the northern half of the big Baltic island and on the small island off it.

se-YK4r.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with four stripes
se-YK4r.summary: Four stripes, sometimes with a woman figure. Finland and Denmark use five stripes. Norway usually four, but can have five.

differs.how: Finland has five stripes
Denmark has five stripes

se-YpBE.title: Houses: older-looking red brick houses
se-YpBE.summary: Many family houses are red brick, a bit older-looking than red brick houses elsewhere. Denmark has lots of red brick too.

se-ZGJn.title: Bollard: wedge-shaped, like Germany
se-ZGJn.summary: Wedge-shaped bollards, like Germany's, mostly in the southern regions.

se-ZI20.title: Rock walls: mostly in the south
se-ZI20.summary: Rock walls are mainly in the south, most on the two big Baltic islands and some coasts. Walls round churches and cemeteries are common further north.

se-ZIJ8.title: Road: wide divided road in flat forest
se-ZIJ8.summary: One E4 stretch in the north is large enough to have a wide ditch or barrier between lanes. Flat, forested with thin birches and pines, getting lower further north.

se-ZdI8.title: Landscape: flat fields, forested hills west
se-ZdI8.summary: Flat fields with a single forested range of hills to the west means east of one lakeside hill in the south-centre.

se-ZesW.title: Bus shelters: black with square ridge on roof back
se-ZesW.summary: Black bus shelters with a square ridge along the back of the roof, found in two cities.

se-aX6G.title: Street signs: two rows split by a black line, no border
se-aX6G.summary: Street signs in the capital have two rows divided by a black line and usually no black border. Rare in one central town. Some suburbs use plain white signs.

se-cfRa.title: Signposts: three yellow stripes
se-cfRa.summary: Three yellow stripes appear on signposts and street lamps in one western town, and on traffic lights in the capital.

se-d2KD.title: Poles: small yellow tree-felling signs
se-d2KD.summary: Small yellow signs advertising tree felling are common on poles and lamp posts in the capital's suburbs, often showing the capital's phone code.

se-dDlG.title: Pole: green snow poles
se-dDlG.summary: Green snow poles occasionally appear around one north-eastern coastal city.

se-dXFB.title: Landscape: round exposed rocks with bushes, west coast
se-dXFB.summary: Round exposed rocks with small bushes on them are common on the west coast. Around the capital, rocks look sharper and often carry thick moss.

se-eFK9.title: Bollard: flat or cylinder with black rectangle
se-eFK9.summary: Flat bollards, or cylinders with a black rectangle holding the reflector, mostly on major roads in the northern half. One flat type looks like the horizontal-band type but its black part isn't horizontal.

se-esbg.title: Signposts: striped markings, red-yellow common
se-esbg.summary: Signposts often have stripes: blue and white, or red and yellow most common. Blue and white also appear in Finland and Estonia, but the other colours don't.

se-f45P.title: Houses: dense rows of tiny red sheds
se-f45P.summary: Dense rows of very small red sheds in coastal towns on the northern west coast.

se-f9QK.title: Cars: Volvo is the most common brand
se-f9QK.summary: Volvo is almost 30% of passenger cars. In Norway and Finland about 10%.

differs.how: Only about 10% Volvos
Only about 10% Volvos

se-fnlS.title: Roofs: square corrugated metal with moss, steep barns
se-fnlS.summary: Square corrugated metal roof panels with moss, mostly on large steep barns, in the south, especially the far south and south-east coast.

se-g8uK.title: Houses: red timber houses, log portals, härbren
se-g8uK.summary: Strong wooden craftsmanship in the central-west: red timbered houses, log portals and distinctive storehouses called härbren. Similar buildings exist elsewhere but are far more common here.

se-gNOV.title: Roads: very red roads and thin pines
se-gNOV.summary: Many roads in the west of one central-west county and nearby are noticeably red. With thin pine forest it points strongly to that region.

se-gTIl.title: Fence: thin vertical trunks with diagonal ones
se-gTIl.summary: Traditional wooden fence of thin, spaced vertical trunks with slightly diagonal trunks stacked on top. Found in Norway near the border too, but much less.

se-gtqn.title: Street signs: like the southern city's but yellow
se-gtqn.summary: Signs like the southern city's but with a yellow background, in one southern coastal town.

se-gwEG.title: Landscape: forested rocky mountains around farm valleys
se-gwEG.summary: Many forested, rocky mountains of different heights surrounding winding farm valleys, on the high coast.

se-hG6f.title: Plants: thin weak-looking trees, sandy soil
se-hG6f.summary: Thin, weak-looking boreal trees and somewhat sandy soil mean the far north.

se-hJxs.title: Pole: many yellow snow poles with two reflectors
se-hJxs.summary: Road 95 closest to Norway has many yellow snow poles with two white reflectors, in Gen 2 autumn or winter, or snowy Gen 4.

se-iQLp.title: Landscape: many small wooden windmills
se-iQLp.summary: Numerous small grey, sometimes red, wooden windmills on one island, which has more windmills than any other region.

se-izD7.title: Landscape: flat open fields with wind turbines
se-izD7.summary: Mostly flat, like the central lake area, but more open and with lots of wind turbines. The forest in the distance is much farther away.

se-jhOZ.title: Coverage: thawing snow in mountains
se-jhOZ.summary: Road 95 west of one northern town shows Gen 4 thawing snow in mountains, with snow decreasing further east.

se-jsad.title: Google car: low Gen 4 'smallcam'
se-jsad.summary: Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. Can be fully see-through. Most of northern Europe has it.

se-ju1G.title: Farming: large orchards
se-ju1G.summary: Most big orchards are around one town on the east coast of the far south. Others are north-east of another town, around one on the west and on the south-east shore of a big lake.

se-ktOj.title: Street names: -gattu or -gatu endings
se-ktOj.summary: Street names ending in gattu or gatu appear in central-west near a big lake: gattu in the south of the area, gatu in the north.

se-l14r.title: Houses: limestone, dirty white, grey stone churches
se-l14r.summary: Houses are limestone with a dirty-looking white facade. Churches are grey, or white with grey corners, with a big portal and small windows split by a pillar.

se-lOhm.title: Language: street names ending in -ween or -weg
se-lOhm.summary: A language only in and around one central-west town, mostly on street signs with names ending in -ween or -weg.

se-leAt.title: Road: small birches, snowy mountains, big lake
se-leAt.summary: The E10 near the Norwegian border has small birches with some pines, snow-covered mountains to the west and all around near the border, and a big lake to the north in the western half.

se-lm-131.title: Road lines: short dashed outer lines
se-lm-131.summary: Short dashed outer lines in a Nordic setting suggest this country. Norway uses long dashes and Finland full lines. Other European countries may have short or medium dashes too.

differs.how: Norway uses long dashed outer lines
Finland uses full outer lines

se-lm-2983.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with four stripes, detailed man
se-lm-2983.summary: Four-stripe pedestrian signs are in Norway, here and Bulgaria. The detailed man without a hat is only here.

differs.how: Norway's figure is not the detailed hatless man
Bulgaria's figure is not the detailed hatless man

se-lm-3312.title: Bus stops: yellow signs, far south
se-lm-3312.summary: The far-south region uses yellow bus signs.

se-lm-3318.title: Bus stops: red signs with ringed SL logo
se-lm-3318.summary: Capital bus stop signs are usually red and carry the SL logo with half-circle rings under the letters.

se-lm-3333.title: Bus stops: red french-horn logo
se-lm-3333.summary: The south-central region's signs show a small red stylised french horn logo, with a similar colour scheme everywhere.

se-lm-3340.title: Bus stops: heart-shaped bus logo, yellow-red buses
se-lm-3340.summary: The south-east coast county has a heart-shaped bus logo and yellow and red buses.

se-lm-3341.title: Bus stops: reclining bus seat logo
se-lm-3341.summary: One southern inland county's buses use a logo shaped like the profile of a reclining bus seat.

se-lm-3342.title: Bus stops: Z in a diamond logo
se-lm-3342.summary: In one mid-north county, buses and stops show a Z inside a diamond, visible from far away even in blurry Gen 2.

se-lm-3343.title: Bus stops: H logo with coastline shape
se-lm-3343.summary: On the south-west coast, the H logo's left side has the rough outline of the county's coast.

se-lm-3344.title: Bus stops: Xtrafik name and big X
se-lm-3344.summary: One east-central bus company is called Xtrafik, on stop signs, and its buses have a big X.

se-lm-3345.title: Bus stops: yellow with green stripes, leaf triangle
se-lm-3345.summary: The big Baltic island's stop signs are yellow with green stripes, and buses sometimes show a triangle of three leaves.

se-lm-3346.title: Bus stops: everything green, green swoosh
se-lm-3346.summary: Bus signs and buses are all green, with a green swoosh logo that looks like a bank's.

se-lm-3347.title: Bus stops: stylised horse logo
se-lm-3347.summary: Bus stop signs and buses carry the county's stylised horse logo with diagonal lines.

se-lm-3348.title: Bus stops: two designs, BlekingeTrafiken
se-lm-3348.summary: The south-east coast county uses two stop designs, and its buses show the company name.

se-lm-3349.title: Bus stops: distinct bus shelters in the far north
se-lm-3349.summary: The far-north county has a current sign and very distinctive, common bus shelters that give the region away from far off.

se-lm-3350.title: Bus stops: lime green, two outward arrows
se-lm-3350.summary: Lime green bus stop signs with a logo of two outward-facing arrows.

se-lm-3351.title: Bus stops: black and yellow, UL logo, red shelters
se-lm-3351.summary: Black and yellow stop signs with a UL logo, and red shelters with red shingle roofs. The neighbouring western county has them with a slightly flatter roof.

se-lm-3352.title: Bus stops: green and yellow shark fin logo
se-lm-3352.summary: A green and yellow shark-fin logo is the clearest feature of stops and buses.

se-lm-3353.title: Bus stops: blue-white, three blue arrows
se-lm-3353.summary: Blue and white signs with three blue arrows like a stylised evergreen tree, plus unique blue wooden bus shelters.

se-lm-3354.title: Bus stops: 'Din Tur' text, green-yellow logo
se-lm-3354.summary: Bus signs and stops everywhere carry the text 'Din Tur' and a green and yellow logo.

se-lm-3355.title: Bus stops: plain white sign with VL logo
se-lm-3355.summary: A simple white sign with just the VL logo. Basic, but recognisable once known.

se-lm-3356.title: Bus stops: checkmark logo
se-lm-3356.summary: The west-coast big region's stop signs show a health-organisation-looking checkmark logo.

se-lm-3357.title: Bus stops: blue signs with LT logo
se-lm-3357.summary: Blue signs with a clear LT logo.

se-mJ0O.title: Bollard: black and white, grey reflector
se-mJ0O.summary: Black-and-white post with a grey reflector, orange near junctions. Shapes are wedge, round, or thin and curved.

se-mRCn.title: Pole: lamp below the top, double bolted
se-mRCn.summary: Lamps on wooden poles hang slightly below the top, fixed with a double bolt. Finland also double bolts, but its lamps sit at the top and are much straighter.

differs.how: Finnish lamps are at the top and much straighter

se-mqbt.title: Street signs: unique blue, two lines
se-mqbt.summary: The whole west-coast city uses these unique blue street signs, nearly always with two lines. Other cities have blue signs in the centre, with a different design.

se-nt94.title: Landscape: coastal road, grassy ridge east
se-nt94.summary: On the southern tip of the big island: a west coastal road with grassy fields and a grassy hill ridge to the east.

se-oUKS.title: Pole: wooden pole with small black cap
se-oUKS.summary: Mostly wooden utility poles with various tops, often with a small black metal cap, found only in Nordic countries. Norway and Finland use mostly wooden poles too.

se-pGFR.title: Landscape: dry stony fields, juniper bushes
se-pGFR.summary: Small, dry stony fields with small juniper bushes on the big Baltic island mean its northern small island. It is more extreme near the north coast.

se-pUwU.title: Plants: mistletoe in trees
se-pUwU.summary: Mistletoe is mostly near the big central lake, very common in one city there.

se-pdD1.title: Landscape: paved road above the treeline
se-pdD1.summary: Most mountain roads stay below the treeline. The only paved road above it, with no trees, is on a county border near the Norwegian border. Coverage is autumn, with yellow-brown plants.

se-q7GI.title: Houses: white stone or brick with coloured gable
se-q7GI.summary: White stone houses, or red brick with a coloured wooden triangle under the roof at the sides, in the far south. Similar houses appear across the southern half.

se-qE6m.title: Landscape: flat, medium fields, bush islands in fields
se-qE6m.summary: Around the big central lake: flat ground, medium fields, forest beyond, and small 'islands' of bushes and trees in the fields.

se-qM5X.title: Chimneys: red brick, crown tops, often painted white
se-qM5X.summary: Red brick chimneys with a crown-like top or wide rectangular holes, near a big lake in the central-west. Often painted white.

se-r30o.title: Pole: wooden marker with blue and white stripes
se-r30o.summary: Wooden electricity markers with a blue and a white stripe at the top, often near poles and pylons. Not found in any other Nordic country.

se-sN4Z.title: Chevron: yellow arrows on blue
se-sN4Z.summary: The only European country with yellow arrows on a blue background. Luxembourg has it very rarely.

se-sdJZ.title: Coverage: spring Gen 4 with dirty thawing snow
se-sdJZ.summary: A northern coastal city has lots of Gen 4 spring coverage, with dirty piles of thawing snow along nearly every road. Almost no other city has this.

se-tJBR.title: Street signs: old white with black corners
se-tJBR.summary: Old-looking white street signs with black corners, all through the southern big city.

se-vHIX.title: Bus stops: three blue stripes
se-vHIX.summary: A west-region bus stop with three blue stripes means one municipality, but the same stripes are on bus stops in the whole neighbouring coastal region.

se-vZOl.title: Phone numbers: 3-4 digit area code, mobiles start 07
se-vZOl.summary: Landline area codes are 3-4 digits (2 in the capital). The third and fourth digits tend to rise to the north-east. Mobile numbers always start with 07.

se-vbvY.title: Landscape: dirt road over a treeless plateau
se-vbvY.summary: The highest public road is a dirt road straight over a treeless plateau, in Gen 4 on a cloudy summer day. The highest point has a parking spot.

se-wkVF.title: Place names: endings by region
se-wkVF.summary: Some place name endings only occur in certain regions, shown on the map. They also cover farms and other places, with some exceptions.

se-wsCX.title: Landscape: flat small fields in the north
se-wsCX.summary: Flat, small or medium fields while in the northern half mean you are likely near the coast between two big northern towns.

se-wyog.title: Signs: bilingual with an indigenous language, far north
se-wyog.summary: Bilingual signs in an indigenous Sámi language appear inland in the north.

se-x5PC.title: Walls: uneven stone brick
se-x5PC.summary: Uneven stone bricks appear in houses and rock walls on one island, and less commonly in rock walls on the other big island.

se-xUYC.title: Fence: wedge-cut trunks
se-xUYC.summary: Traditional fences use thin round trunks, but on the big Baltic island they use bigger trunks cut into sharp wedges.

se-yImG.title: Road lines: short white dashed outer lines
se-yImG.summary: On smaller roads the outer lines are white and dashed, clearly shorter than Norway's. All lines are white, unlike Norway and Finland.

differs.how: Norwegian dashes are longer, and lines can be yellow
Finland has yellow lines

se-zQ9U.title: Pole: mix of orange and yellow snow poles
se-zQ9U.summary: A mix of orange and yellow snow poles in mountains means road E10 near the Norwegian border.

se-zbLV.title: Landscape: treeless mountain tops, north-west
se-zbLV.summary: Mountains with no trees at the top are only in the north-west. Forested mountains appear in several regions.

se-zhtp.title: Street signs: blue, one line
se-zhtp.summary: Blue street signs like the west-coast city's but usually with one line instead of two, in one southern municipality.

se-zim3.title: Road: brown-red wet pavement, thin pines and birches
se-zim3.summary: One E45 stretch has brown-red wet pavement with thin pines and birches along the road.
